newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bank bills pummelled as currency slides.
newsitem.headline: NZ bank bills pummelled as currency slides.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 92.71 (PREV 92.85) 90-DAYS 7.76 (PREV 7.57)
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.70 PCT (PREV 8.00) US 5-YR 6.15 (PREV 6.16)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 766.87 (PREV 765.70) Reuters NZ MCI -58 vs -60
New Zealand bank bills took another pounding on Wednesday as traders struggled to keep the monetary index near the desired level as the currency slid.
The 90-day bank bill rate rose to 7.76 percent compared with its 7.57 percent close on Tuesday.
The New Zealand dollar at one stage lost over half a U.S. cent to hit an 18-month low and that put pressure on the MCI.
The index ended 58 basis points easier than the Reserve Bank desires and traders are wary the bank will act to bring it into line.
All eyes will be on the New Zealand dollar and U.S./yen rate overnight to see if that will put further pressure on interest rates.
Dealers said the market closed with a bid tone in the bills and currency but there had been a general flight away from currencies such as the New Zealand and Australian dollars.

Some dealers said the Reserve Bank will be watching data on retail sales, unemployment, and building plus two confidence surveys over the next two days to assess if the economy is really weaker than the RB has projected.
"Recession, here we come," quipped one dealer about the dramatic recent rise in short-term rates.
He noted short-term interest rates had risen 90 basis points from a point when Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash had assessed the economy as weak and inflation under control
There was heavy disinvestment overnight and nearly all the trading was coming from one direction.
